title: Signed shift, associator and symmetry identities on total cochain tensors
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small relative to the universe of its ordinary module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with $\mathcal O$ commutative. Use integer-indexed cochain complexes, $E[a]^p=E^{p+a}$ and $d_{E[a]}=(-1)^a d_E$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the direct-sum total tensor $T(E,F)$ with differential $d(x\otimes y)=dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For arbitrary, possibly unbounded complexes $E,F,G$ and integers $a,b,c$, the summand formulas
$$t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}:T(E[a],F[b])\xrightarrow{\sim}T(E,F)[a+b],\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto(-1)^{bp}x\otimes y\quad(x\in E[a]^p,\ y\in F[b]^q),$$
$$\alpha^{\rm Ch}:T(T(E,F),G)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(E,T(F,G)),\qquad (x\otimes y)\otimes z\longmapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z),$$
$$\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E,F}:T(E,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(F,E),\qquad x\otimes y\longmapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x\quad(x\in E^p,\ y\in F^q)$$
define natural chain isomorphisms, uniquely specified by these summand formulas. In terms of the integer bifunctor shift comparisons $s^1,s^2$ of the additive bifunctor $\otimes_{\mathcal O}$ [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], $t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}=s^1_a(E,F)[b]\circ s^2_b(E[a],F)$, since $s^2_b$ multiplies the summand of first-factor degree $p$ by $(-1)^{bp}$ and $s^1_a$ is unsigned. The inverse of $t^{\rm Ch}$ has the same scalar on the reverse reindexing, the inverse associator is reverse reassociation, and the inverse symmetry is $\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{F,E}$.

With ordinary reassociation and the canonical equalities of shift indices understood, the following are identities of natural chain maps:
$$t^{\rm Ch}_{a+b,c}\circ T(t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b},1)=t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b+c}\circ T(1,t^{\rm Ch}_{b,c}),$$
as maps from the triple shifted tensor to $T(E,T(F,G))[a+b+c]$, with the appropriate $\alpha^{\rm Ch}$ on the source and the shifted target, and
$$\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E,F}[a+b]\circ t^{\rm Ch}_{a,b}=(-1)^{ab}t^{\rm Ch}_{b,a}\circ\sigma^{\rm Ch}_{E[a],F[b]}.$$
On shifted triple degree $(p,q,r)$ the two shift-extraction coefficients in the first identity are $(-1)^{bp+c(p+q)}$ and $(-1)^{cq+(b+c)p}$, respectively. On shifted bidegree $(p,q)$ the two coefficients in the second identity are $(-1)^{bp+(p+a)(q+b)}$ and $(-1)^{ab+pq+aq}$, respectively. These formulas hold for negative as well as positive integers. No flatness, localization, or degree-zero source is assumed.
